userStories.title: Harden telegram-agent scheduled task against silent process death
userStories.description: As the operator, I need the Telegram-LLM bot to not silently die again — earlier this session its ONLOGON-triggered process was found dead with no crash log entry after being alive at startup, and had to be manually re-triggered via schtasks /run.
acceptanceCriteria: Read telegram-agent/bot.mjs, telegram-agent/start-bot.ps1, and this session's earlier finding about the silent process death (schtasks showed 'Ready' not 'Running', zero matching node process, no crash line in the log) before changing anything

Add a restart-on-exit wrapper: either a loop inside start-bot.ps1 that relaunches node if it exits (with a backoff and a max-restarts-per-hour cap so a crash-loop doesn't spin forever), or register the scheduled task with a restart trigger via schtasks — pick whichever is simpler and actually verifiable

Live-verify: kill the current bot.mjs node process for real, confirm the new restart mechanism actually relaunches it within a reasonable window (under 2 minutes), and confirm via a real getMe-equivalent check that it's alive and responding again
Do not weaken the existing security posture (chat-id + sender-id pinning, --strict-mcp-config, token scrubbing, rate limiting) while making this change
node --check telegram-agent/bot.mjs passes; PowerShell script has no syntax errors
